name: Vitoria-Gasteiz (Spain)
description: White field with a red saltire, charged at the centre with the crowned arms of Vitoria-Gasteiz (a castle with two crows on a green mount).
history: The flag of Vitoria is white, crossed by a red saltire, and flies solemnly on the façade of the city hall on special occasions, with the arms of Vitoria at the centre. The present flag was chosen in 1922 following a proposal by the writer José Colá y Goiti, who presented it in 1918 with a first design in which the arms of the saltire of Saint Andrew were one blue and one red, representing the bourgeois and working classes, although the classic red also adopted in other nearby cities was finally chosen. The previous flag of Vitoria dated from 1835: embroidered with the arms of Vitoria on a white field, it was a gift of Isabella II to the Urban Militia of Vitoria for not letting the city fall into Carlist hands.
